title: Owner Authorization
description: Experimental (media_buy.social_profiles). Operator-attested evidence that the owner of a platform account connected an operator to that account. With method platform_oauth, the operator holds an OAuth grant that the account owner approved on the platform, and the grant resolves to the account named here. The record is the operator's own statement: buyers cannot check the grant, so it is weaker than an adagents.json the owner publishes on a domain the owner controls. It shows the owner connected the operator; it is not by itself a sales mandate, which still comes from the brand.json and adagents.json chain. An operator MUST remove the record when the grant is revoked or stops resolving to the account. Buyers weigh it under their own policy, as described in the platform OAuth evidence section of the collections documentation.

method.description: How the operator holds the owner's authorization. platform_oauth: an OAuth grant the account owner approved on the platform that hosts the account. Consumers MUST ignore records with a method they do not recognize.

platform_domain.description: Registrable domain of the platform that issued the grant and hosts the account. Same value as publisher_domain on the matching collection distribution entry.

account.description: The platform account the grant resolves to. On a property, it MUST equal one of the property's identifiers. On a collection, it MUST equal an identifier on the distribution entry whose publisher_domain equals platform_domain.

type.description: Identifier type of the account, for example youtube_channel_id

verified_by.description: The operator that holds the grant. Its brand.json identifies the operator, and buyers compare it with the selling agent's operator.

verified_at.description: When the operator last confirmed the grant was live, for example by a successful API call made as the account. Buyers MAY treat a record whose verified_at is older than their policy allows as absent.

granted_scopes.description: The platform's own names for the scopes the owner granted, as the platform reports them. Lets a buyer see whether the grant covers more than reading analytics. Informational; AdCP defines no scope vocabulary.
